query: GPU compute shortage or oversupply rental price news

results.title: Amazon is hiking chip-rental prices and reportedly moving Nvidia processors off the balance sheet
highlights:
In a sign of the financing crunch facing the hyperscalers backing the AI revolution, Amazon has announced it is raising prices on how much it charges to rent high-performance microchips as it reportedly is going to sell and then lease back Nvidia chips.

Amazon AMZN on Friday said it is raising prices, by about 15%, starting next week, for what’s called EC2 Capacity Blocks, which provide access to computing power on Nvidia chips ranging from the older A100 to the newer, more high-performance B300.

results.title: Why Hyperscalers Need Nebius (And Not The Other Way Around) (NASDAQ:NBIS) | Seeking Alpha
highlights:
- Nebius rents 12 of its 16 sites, so it avoids the conversion costs and multi-year timelines of competing ex-crypto miners, and monetizes faster.
- GPU rental prices are rising about 20% this month (B300: from $8.10 to $9.70 per hour), and short-term auctions close at $40-50M per MW versus $20-25M for long-term contracts.
- Q2 revenue grew 454% YoY to $582M versus 251% for costs, though losses persist due to depreciation and heavy CAPEX. I believe that at this pace, profitability is a matter of time.
- Hyperscalers building their own capacity (even to rent out the surplus) is the main threat, but as long as compute stays scarce, they depend on Nebius's speed.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
highlights:
Renting one NVIDIA H100 for an hour costs $3.49 on Runpod and $12.29 on Microsoft Azure — the same chip, listed on public pricing pages on October 2, 2026. Axis Intelligence Research’s GPU Hour Premium Ratio puts the hyperscaler list premium at 2.93x the neocloud median, and AWS is raising every GPU Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7.

## Quick Answer

How much does a GPU cost in October 2026? In the cloud, an NVIDIA H100 lists between $3.49 and $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand; the neocloud median is $3.99. A B200 lists from $6.69 to $8.60. On the consumer side, the cheapest new RTX 5070 on Newegg was $869.99 against a $549 launch price — 58% above MSRP.

...

1. According to Axis Intelligence Research, hyperscalers list the NVIDIA H100 at 2.93 times the neocloud median price — $11.68 versus $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, as of October 2, 2026 (GPU Hour Premium Ratio, GHPR).
2. AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU rates about 15% effective October 7, 2026, taking an H100 accelerator-hour from $5.191 to $5.970 and a B200 from $12.355 to $14.208, per AWS’s pricing page.
3. An 8-GPU H100 server rented on-demand for three years costs $2.58 million on Azure and $734,000 on Runpod, according to Axis Intelligence Research’s list-price TCO calculation.
4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.
5. Azure’s spot price for an 8x H100 VM is 82% below its own on-demand rate — $18.17 versus $98.32 per hour in US East, per Microsoft’s Retail Prices API.

...

### H100 on-demand price per GPU-hour by provider (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Instance / SKU | Listed price | GPUs | Price per GPU-hour | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod | H100 SXM Pod (Secure Cloud) | $3.49/hr | 1 | $3.49 | Runpod pricing |
| Lambda | NVIDIA H100 SXM instance | $3.99/GPU/hr | 1–8 | $3.99 | Lambda pricing |
| CoreWeave | NVIDIA HGX H100 (North America) | $49.24/hr | 8 | $6.16 | CoreWeave pricing |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g, us-central1 | $88.49/hr | 8 | $11.06 | Google Cloud accelerator-optimized pricing |
| Microsoft Azure | ND96isr H100 v5, East US | $98.32/hr | 8 | $12.29 | Azure Retail Prices API |

...

That is the number most “GPU price” pages quote, and it overstates the useful comparison, because Runpod’s $3.49 Pod and Azure’s $98.32 VM are not the same product.

...

### AWS EC2 Capacity Block rate change, effective October 7, 2026

| Instance family | GPU | Rate before (per accelerator-hour) | Rate from Oct 7, 2026 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.040 | $16.146 | +15.0% |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 | +15.0% |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 | +15.0% |
| P5e | H200 | $5.970 | $6.866 | +15.0% |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191 | $5.970 | +15.0% |
| P4de | A100 80GB | $2.214 | $2.546 | +15.0% |
| P4d | A100 40GB | $1.475 | $1.696 | +15.0% |

...

A uniform 15% move across seven GPU generations — including a 2020-era A100 40GB — tells you this is not a scarcity signal about one chip. Capacity Blocks are AWS’s mechanism for guaranteed short-term cluster access, and a flat repricing across the whole catalog reads as AWS re-pricing guaranteed availability itself. Buyers who only need interruptible capacity should read this as a reason to look at spot and neocloud rates, not as proof that GPUs in general got 15% more expensive.

...

### H100 price per GPU-hour by commitment model (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Model | Price per GPU-hour | vs. same provider on-demand |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure (East US) | On-demand | $12.29 | — |
| Azure (East US) | 1-year reservation ($551,221 per VM) | $7.87 | −36% |
| Azure (East US) | 3-year reservation ($1,134,310 per VM) | $5.40 | −56% |
| Azure (East US) | Spot ($18.17/hr per VM) | $2.27 | −82% |
| Google Cloud (us-central1) | On-demand | $11.06 | — |
| Google Cloud | 1-year resource CUD | $7.67 | −31% |
| Google Cloud | 3-year resource CUD | $4.86 | −56% |
| Google Cloud | DWS Flex-start | $4.79 | −57% |
| Google Cloud | Spot | $6.62 | −40% |
| CoreWeave | Spot ($19.71/hr per 8 GPUs) | $2.46 | −60% |

Per-GPU-hour = VM price ÷ 8. Azure reservation per-hour = total term price ÷ (term years × 8,760 hours) ÷ 8. All Axis Intelligence Research calculations from vendor list prices.

...

### Axis Intelligence Research cloud TCO: one 8x H100 node, list price, 100% utilization

| Provider and model | 1 year | 3 years |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Azure, on-demand | $861,283 | $2,583,850 |
| Google Cloud, on-demand | $775,172 | $2,325,517 |
| Azure, 1-yr / 3-yr reservation (term price) | $551,221 | $1,134,310 |
| CoreWeave, on-demand | $431,342 | $1,294,027 |
| AWS Capacity Block, rate from Oct 7, 2026 | $418,378 | $1,255,133 |
| Google Cloud, 3-year resource CUD | $340,452 | $1,021,356 |
| Lambda, on-demand ($3.99 × 8) | $279,619 | $838,858 |
| Runpod, on-demand ($3.49 × 8) | $244,579 | $733,738 |

...

## What Moves GPU Prices?

Who you rent from. The single largest variable in the data above. Same chip, 3.5x price range on list.

How much availability you’re buying. Guaranteed cluster capacity (Capacity Blocks, 1-Click Clusters, reservations) is priced above interruptible capacity — sometimes above plain on-demand, as Lambda’s B200 shows.

Bundled host resources. Hyperscaler VMs include large vCPU, RAM and local-SSD allocations in the GPU price. A Google Cloud a3-highgpu-8g bundles 208 vCPUs and 1,871 GB of memory; you pay for them whether your job uses them or not.

Commitment length. Three-year commitments cut Azure and Google Cloud H100 list prices by 56%.

Memory supply. On the consumer side, graphics card prices above launch MSRP track the cost and availability of GDDR7, which competes for production capacity with the HBM used in data-center GPUs.

results.title: GPU Rental Rates Double as Infrastructure Costs Offset AI Efficiency Gains | Tech Pulse | TheNextGenTechInsider
highlights:
GPU rental prices have doubled to $8.08 per hour due to rising infrastructure and energy constraints. Despite this, rapid gains in AI efficiency and new hardware like NVIDIA Blackwell continue to drive performance.

...

GPU rental prices have doubled over the last six months, increasing from $4.40 to $8.08 per GPU-hour, even as the cost of AI inference continues to decrease, according to analysis by Tom Tunguz. This divergence is driven by escalating data center construction costs and critical energy constraints that offset the economic benefits of improved AI efficiency.

The rise in compute costs is attributed to the increasing price of essential infrastructure components, including concrete, copper, and credit. Furthermore, electricity remains a significant bottleneck for scaling; for instance, Oracle recently invoked force majeure at its New Mexico campus following a six-month delay in natural gas pipeline delivery.

...

Despite rising hardware costs, AI efficiency is improving at a rate that mitigates the expense. A specific benchmark threshold that required $0.55 eighteen months ago now clears for just $0.0015, representing a 377x reduction in cost Tom Tunguz.

results.title: Amazon raises GPU rents 15% while shifting $8 billion of chips off its books · The Inference
highlights:
Amazon lifts reserved GPU rates about 15% on 7 October, taking the eight-H100 hour toward $47.76, while moving $8 billion of Grace Blackwell chips toward a debt-funded vehicle. Renters pay shortage prices; the bond buyers would hold the chips.

...

Book eight Nvidia▼−3.21% — Nvidia, down 3.21 percent today H100s on AWS for a training run and the bill is $41.528 an hour in major US regions 1. On 2 October Amazon▼−1.16% — Amazon, down 1.16 percent today said that rate, and the rest of its EC2 Capacity Blocks for machine learning, goes up about 15% next week, on chips from the older A100 to the B300 2.

At the announced rise, the eight-H100 p5.48xlarge hour steps up to about $47.76 on 7 October 3. Capacity Blocks book up to eight weeks ahead 3: reserve before then, or budget the raise.

...

Renters see shortage. The balance sheet sees something else. Amazon has approached outside investors to move about $8 billion of Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside debt and lease them back, keeping up to 10% of the equity; the chips already run at more than a dozen sites across five US states 1. One report ties the structure↗ to protecting Amazon's credit rating 4; Amazon and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment 1.

The backdrop is the ramp: 2026 capex is set at $200 billion against $131 billion last year, carried by a $17.5 billion term loan, a debut £4.25 billion sterling bond and nearly $100 billion of bond sales, the most among hyperscalers 1. Q2 capex ran $53.1 billion against $45.4 billion of operating cash, with free cash flow negative in both quarters of 2026 5.

...

On demand, the same eight H100s cost less outside the reservation: Nebius▼−12.27% — Nebius, down 12.27 percent today lifted its H100 rate 17% to $4.50 a GPU-hour on 1 October, so eight run $36.00 against AWS's $41.53, about a 15% premium for the guaranteed hour 6. That premium is measured against today's AWS rate; after 7 October it widens to roughly a third. The glut case is not in this record, and on-demand rates are rising too. What moves is residual value: if the chips age badly, the loss lands on the SPV's debt holders, not on Amazon.

...

Watch the SPV: the spread on $8 billion of chip-backed debt is the market's first posted price for a used Blackwell. The rent is set by the landlord. The residual is somebody else's problem.

Business takeaway

Amazon is charging renters shortage prices for GPUs while selling the chips' residual risk to bond buyers. The spread on the $8 billion chip-backed vehicle will be the market's first posted price for a used Blackwell.

results.title: Compute Just Became a Tradeable Asset — What the GPU Shortage Means for Your Business
highlights:
If you've tried to reserve GPU capacity for an AI workload in the past two months, you've likely felt it firsthand: prices climbing, lead times stretching, and availability drying up just when demand is highest. This isn't a temporary blip. It's a structural shift in how compute gets bought, sold, and priced — and it's happening faster than most businesses can adapt to.

## The Numbers Behind the Squeeze

GPU rental prices for Nvidia's Blackwell chips have hit $4.08 per hour, up 48% in just 60 days. High-bandwidth memory is effectively sold out into 2027. H100 and H200 lead times are running 36 to 52 weeks, driven by constrained packaging capacity and surging memory demand that outpaces what suppliers can produce. Bank of America projects demand will outstrip supply through 2029 — this isn't a problem that resolves itself next quarter.

The shortage has already caused visible disruption at the frontier: compute constraints have been cited in outages and forced product delays at some of the largest AI labs in the world. If the companies building the models are feeling the pinch, every business building on top of them is feeling it too.

...

The clearest signal of how serious this has gotten: in October 2026, CME Group and Silicon Data launched cash-settled futures contracts on H100 and B200 rental pricing. That's not a niche financial product — it's an acknowledgment that compute capacity now behaves like oil, wheat, or electricity. It has volatile pricing, real scarcity, and enough institutional demand that finance teams need a way to hedge it.

...

- Reserved capacity increasingly goes to whoever can commit the largest, longest contracts — squeezing out startups and mid-size teams who need flexibility, not year-long lock-ins.
- Unpredictable pricing makes it hard to budget AI initiatives with any confidence, especially for teams scaling usage gradually rather than all at once.
- Waiting in line isn't a strategy. A 36-to-52-week lead time on dedicated hardware means most businesses need another way to access compute when they need it, not when a reservation finally clears.
- The businesses that adapt fastest are the ones treating compute access itself as something to actively manage, not something to assume will always be there.

results.title: Musk's Colossus idles at 11% and rents to the rivals it was built to beat · The Inference
highlights:
SpaceX's Colossus, the Memphis cluster built in 122 days, runs near 11% utilization while Anthropic and Google rent its machines for a combined $2.2 billion a month. Both flagship leases carry 90-day exits, and that is the soft spot in a $41 billion leasing run-rate.

...

Colossus 1 rose from a defunct Electrolux site in Memphis and opened in July 2024, 122 days after construction began, carrying about 100,000 NVIDIA▼−3.21% — NVIDIA, down 3.21 percent today H100s 1. Research circulated on 1 October↗ puts SpaceXAI's fleet of nearly 550,000 GPUs at about 11% utilization, with some 60,000 chips active at Colossus 1 as of May; the figure is single-source 2. Training moved to Colossus 2 2. The old machine's biggest tenant is now Anthropic PVT$350B — Anthropic, private, latest valuation $350B, the lab Grok was built to chase 2 3.

...

Anthropic contracted all of Colossus 1, about 220,000 GPUs, at $1.25 billion a month through May 2029; its leaked IPO prospectus↗ sizes the commitment at up to $84.5 billion 2 3. Google takes 110,000 GPUs at Colossus 2 for $920 million a month through June 2029, a deal SpaceX▼−2.57% — SpaceX, down 2.57 percent today disclosed in a June regulatory filing↗ 4.

Reflection AI PVT$2.1B — Reflection AI, private, latest valuation $2.1B pays $150 million and an unnamed client is due from December at $1.11 billion 5. Together the four sum to $3.4 billion a month, matching the $41.1 billion annualized lease revenue reported in September 5.

...

The fine print is the story. The bulk of Anthropic's commitment is cancelable on 90 days' notice, unlike its firmer deals with Google, Amazon▼−1.16% — Amazon, down 1.16 percent today and Microsoft▼−0.28% — Microsoft, down 0.28 percent today 3. Google's lease can be ended by either party on 90 days' notice after this year, and SpaceX had to deliver the committed GPUs by 30 September or hand Google an exit after a month's grace 4. A lease either side can end inside a quarter is a quarterly rental with a multi-year headline. Tenants paid anyway, for whoever "could turn on 200,000 GPUs overnight", in ClusterMax analyst Jordan Nanos's estimate 7.

...

Second-quarter capex ran $18.4 billion against $7.8 billion of revenue↗, after $10.1 billion in the first quarter, when the AI segment lost $2.5 billion on $818 million of sales 8 4. Colossus has absorbed more than $35.8 billion 1.

Elon Musk counts 110,000 GB200s and 440,000 GB300s at Colossus 2, with 220,000 more "fully operational next week", another batch in November and, "if we get lucky", a third by late December 7. Some sites ran months without backup power or cooling↗, and outages interrupted training 6.

...

The loser is whoever marks the $41.1 billion run-rate as locked multi-year revenue 5. The neoclouds, CoreWeave▼−8.55% — CoreWeave, down 8.55 percent today and Nebius▼−12.27% — Nebius, down 12.27 percent today, hold the pricing case: tenants paid roughly triple going rates to jump the queue 7, and three more batches of 220,000 chips arrive by December to chase the same buyers 1.

results.title: Reflection AI locked up to $7.3 billion of GPU rent inside a token price war · The Inference
highlights:
The ex-DeepMind lab's two 2026 contracts, a $6.3 billion ceiling at SpaceX and a reported $1 billion-plus with Nebius, add to more than $7 billion of rent through 2029. The open-weight market it sells into cut token prices 23% in August alone.

...

Reflection AI PVT$2.1B — Reflection AI, private, latest valuation $2.1B, founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers, signed its first compute contract on 22 June↗: $150 million a month from 1 July 2026 through 2029, for Nvidia▼−3.21% — Nvidia, down 3.21 percent today GB300 capacity at SpaceX's▼−2.57% — SpaceX, down 2.57 percent today Colossus 2 site near Memphis. The deal is worth up to $6.3 billion, and either side can end it on 90 days' notice once the first three months pass 1.

...

Nebius, which confirmed the Reflection deal, booked $582.3 million of second-quarter revenue, up 454%↗, on a $37.5 billion backlog 9 10, and lifted its year-end contracted-power target from above 3 gigawatts to 5 10. Microsoft▼−0.28% — Microsoft, down 0.28 percent today has committed up to $19.4 billion and Meta▲+2.23% — Meta, up 2.23 percent today up to $27 billion, and executives call existing capacity essentially sold out 2 4.

On 1 October, Nebius's on-demand GPU rates rise as much as 21% under a customer notice↗ 11. SpaceX's AI division lost $6.35 billion last year; Reflection's monthly check sits beside Anthropic's $1.25 billion and Google's $920 million, all on cancelable terms 1 5.

...

On 21 September, Rothschild & Co Redburn started Nebius and CoreWeave at Sell↗ anyway, citing falling GPU rental prices, hyperscalers scaling captive fleets, and rising financing costs 9 3. On Nebius's own filings, second-quarter capex of $5.65 billion ran about 9.7 times revenue of $582 million 12. The October increase answers the first charge directly.

...

Reflection AI has committed up to $7.3 billion to GPU rent through 2029 against about $2.6 billion raised, while the open-weight market it sells into cut token prices 23% in August. The landlords are booked out and raising rates; the 90-day cancellation window is the tell.

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% - Economic Frame
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

...

| Nvidia GPU | Prior on-demand column | Announced October 1 card | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HGX H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +$0.65, or 16.9% |
| HGX H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +$0.90, or 20.0% |
| HGX B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +$1.35, or 18.9% |
| HGX B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +$1.65, or 21.0% |

Reuters’ “17% to 21%” is this range, with 16.9% rounded up. “Up to 21%” is the B300. The smaller H100 move is the one that changes the reading. Hopper is not the generation Nvidia is leading with.

...

Put the H100 on a bill. Eight GPUs go from $30.80 an hour to $36.00. Over a 720-hour month the list charge goes from $22,176 to $25,920. An 8-GPU B300 box moves from $45,216 to $54,720. Those are walk-up numbers, before tax, storage, or a commitment discount, and they are not invoices.

...

CoreWeave did not publish an H100 card. On September 17 it published a contract print. The release, carried on Nasdaq, says that since June 30, 2026, CoreWeave has continued to contract new compute at higher prices. In the third quarter it has signed short-dated contracts of about three to six months, “with pricing of approximately $40 million per megawatt, calculated as annualized revenue divided by power required to service the related clusters.”

...

A glut runs the other way. The owner of empty halls cuts the rate to fill them. Nebius is adding halls and raising the walk-up rate in the same season.

...

The tapes diverge on how much of the shortage is already in the price. Nvidia is near its 52-week high. CoreWeave, with short deals near $40 million a megawatt, is still more than 40% off its high, and Nebius is about 23% off its own. The rental power has not been a straight line into the neocloud stocks. It is a straight line into the case that the chip vendor still owns the bottleneck.

...

A glut would show up first in the old chip’s posted hour, or in a paper substitute for that hour. GPU futures have not become a deep hedge. The contract talk has stalled on delivery windows and a long hold, which is what you get when the physical card is still the scarce object. ... Cheaper H100 hours would make that backlog the problem. ... October’s cards say queue.
